::: {#exr-prac-score-zero}
#### Score at the MLE (adapted from @dobson4e, Chapter 3)

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n \siid \Pois(\rate)$.

**(a)** Write the log-likelihood $\ell(\rate; \vx)$.

**(b)** Derive the score function $\ell'(\rate; \vx)$.

**(c)** Show that $\hat\rate_{ML} = \bar{x}$,
and verify that the score equals zero at the MLE.

**(d)** Provide an intuitive interpretation:
why does the score being zero at $\hat\rate_{ML}$ make sense?
:::

:::{#sol-prac-score-zero}

**(a)**

$$
\ba
\ell(\rate; \vx)
&= \logf{\prod_{i=1}^n \frac{\rate^{x_i} e^{-\rate}}{x_i!}}
&& \text{(log of the likelihood of an $\iid$ sample)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \logf{\frac{\rate^{x_i} e^{-\rate}}{x_i!}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{\logf{\rate^{x_i} e^{-\rate}} - \logf{x_i!}}
&& \text{(log of a quotient)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{\logf{\rate^{x_i}} + \logf{e^{-\rate}} - \logf{x_i!}}
&& \text{(log of a product)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{x_i \logf{\rate} + \logf{e^{-\rate}} - \logf{x_i!}}
&& \text{(log of a power)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n \paren{x_i \logf{\rate} - \rate - \logf{x_i!}}
&& \text{($\log$ undoes $\exp$)}
\\
&= \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \logf{\rate} - \sum_{i=1}^n \rate - \sum_{i=1}^n \logf{x_i!}
&& \text{(split the sum)}
\\
&= \paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\logf{\rate} - \sum_{i=1}^n \rate - \sum_{i=1}^n \logf{x_i!}
&& \text{(factor $\logf{\rate}$ out of the first sum)}
\\
&= \paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\logf{\rate} - n\rate - \sum_{i=1}^n \logf{x_i!}
&& \text{(sum of $n$ copies of $\rate$)}
\ea
$$

**(b)**

$$
\ba
\ell'(\rate; \vx)
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\logf{\rate} - n\rate - \sum_{i=1}^n \logf{x_i!}}
&& \text{(log-likelihood from (a))}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\logf{\rate}} - \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rate}
   - \deriv{\rate}\sb{\sum_{i=1}^n \logf{x_i!}}
&& \text{(linearity of differentiation)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\logf{\rate}} - \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rate} - 0
&& \text{(derivative of a constant)}
\\
&= \deriv{\rate}\sb{\paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\logf{\rate}} - \deriv{\rate}\sb{n\rate}
&& \text{(drop the zero term)}
\\
&= \paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\deriv{\rate}\logf{\rate} - n\deriv{\rate}\rate
&& \text{(constant multiple rule)}
\\
&= \paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\rate^{-1} - n\deriv{\rate}\rate
&& \text{(derivative of $\log$)}
\\
&= \paren{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}\rate^{-1} - n
&& \text{(derivative of $\rate$ with respect to itself)}
\\
&= \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n x_i}{\rate} - n
&& \text{(write the negative power as a fraction)}
\\
&= \frac{n\bar{x}}{\rate} - n
&& \text{($\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^n x_i = n\bar{x}$)}
\ea
$$

**(c)**

Setting $\ell'(\rate; \vx) = 0$:

$$
\ba
0 &= \frac{n\bar{x}}{\rate} - n
&& \text{(score from (b))}
\\
\frac{n\bar{x}}{\rate} &= n
&& \text{(add $n$ to both sides)}
\\
n\bar{x} &= n\rate
&& \text{(multiply both sides by $\rate$)}
\\
\hat\rate_{ML} &= \bar{x}
&& \text{(divide both sides by $n$)}
\ea
$$

If $\bar{x} > 0$
(equivalently,
at least one $x_i > 0$),
then

$$
\ba
\ell'(\bar{x}; \vx)
&= \frac{n\bar{x}}{\bar{x}} - n
&& \text{(score from (b) at $\rate = \bar{x}$)}
\\
&= n - n
&& \text{(cancel $\bar{x}$, since $\bar{x} > 0$)}
\\
&= 0
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

If instead all $x_i = 0$,
then $\bar{x} = 0$ and $\hat\rate_{ML} = 0$ is a boundary value.
In that case,
the score formula
$\ell'(\rate; \vx) = \frac{n\bar{x}}{\rate} - n$
is not defined at $\rate = 0$,
so the usual interior verification
$\ell'(\hat\rate_{ML}; \vx) = 0$
does not apply.

**(d)**

The score measures the rate of change of the log-likelihood.
When it equals zero,
increasing or decreasing $\rate$ slightly would not improve the fit;
we are at a "flat" point.
Intuitively,
$\hat\rate_{ML} = \bar{x}$ is the value of $\rate$ that makes
the expected count per observation ($\rate$) exactly equal to
the observed average count ($\bar{x}$).

:::
